about: Source check of the reference text of bank2.json entries 18 to 35, run by the team's audit tooling on 2026-10-18 by fetching each cited page and comparing it with the reference. This is not a human review. Statuses follow the cited page only: supports = the page states the same number or rule; partially = the page states part of it; the version of each law in force in October 2026 was compared where the cited link points to another version.

fields.via: set when the cited link needs JavaScript (www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/...): the same act was read from the official fedlex filestore HTML of the consolidation in force in October 2026
fields.quote: at most one sentence, original language of the page that was read; '...' marks left-out words

hypotheses.claim_checked: AVIG Art. 17(2): register in person as early as possible and at the latest on the first day benefits are claimed; Art. 10(3): unemployed only once registered; ZH: benefits at the earliest from the registration date, register during the notice period; ZH and AG: job search required during the notice period.

sources.where: AVIG Art. 17 Abs. 2 and Art. 10 Abs. 3 (consolidation of 1 Jan 2026, in force Oct 2026)
sources.quote: Die versicherte Person muss sich möglichst frühzeitig, spätestens jedoch am ersten Tag, für den sie Arbeitslosenentschädigung beansprucht, persönlich zur Arbeitsvermittlung anmelden und von da an die Kontrollvorschriften des Bundesrates befolgen.

sources.where: section 'Anmeldung RAV', 'Wann anmelden?'
sources.quote: Leistungen der Arbeitslosenversicherung (ALV) können Sie frühestens ab dem Datum beziehen, an dem Sie sich beim RAV angemeldet haben.

sources.where: section 'Anmeldung beim RAV'
sources.quote: Wichtig: Sie müssen sich bereits während der Kündigungsfrist intensiv um eine neue Arbeitsstelle bemühen.

hypotheses.note: The ZH page also says to register during the notice period and that job search is required during the notice period; the AG page also states that benefits start at the earliest on the registration date.

hypotheses.claim_checked: AVIG: 12 months of contributions within 2 years (Art. 9, 13); 80% daily allowance, 70% without children under 25, full allowance over CHF 140 and no IV pension of 40%+ (Art. 22); 5 waiting days, 10-20 for higher earners without children (Art. 18); at most 260, 400 or 520 allowances (Art. 27).

sources.where: AVIG Art. 9 Abs. 1-3, Art. 13 Abs. 1, Art. 18 Abs. 1, Art. 22 Abs. 1-2, Art. 27 Abs. 2 (consolidation of 1 Jan 2026, in force Oct 2026)
sources.quote: Ein volles Taggeld beträgt 80 Prozent des versicherten Verdienstes.

hypotheses.note: Art. 18(1): 10, 15 or 20 waiting days apply to people without maintenance duties toward children under 25 with insured earnings of CHF 60,001-90,000, 90,001-125,000 and over 125,000. Art. 27(2): 260 allowances with 12 months, 400 with 18 months, 520 with at least 22 months and age 55+ or an IV pension of 40%+; the reference leaves out the lower caps (90 for people exempt from contributions, 180 after loss of an IV pension, 200 for people up to 25 without children). Art. 22(3) lets the Federal Council adjust the CHF 140 threshold; the statute text in force still says 140 and the ordinance was not checked.

hypotheses.claim_checked: BüV Art. 6: spoken B1 and written A2 in a national language; proof by mother tongue, 5 years of compulsory school, completed upper-secondary or tertiary education in a national language, or a certificate from a test meeting recognised quality standards.

sources.where: BüV Art. 6 Abs. 1-2 (consolidation of 1 Aug 2026; Abs. 2 let. d in this wording since 1 Jan 2019)
sources.quote: Die Bewerberin oder der Bewerber muss in einer Landessprache mündliche Sprachkompetenzen mindestens auf dem Referenzniveau B1 und schriftliche Sprachkompetenzen mindestens auf dem Referenzniveau A2 des in Europa allgemein anerkannten Referenzrahmens für Sprachen nachweisen.

sources.where: section 'Sprachanforderungen bei Aufenthalt in der Schweiz' (page last changed 30.08.2026)
sources.quote: Sie muss bei der Einreichung des Gesuchs schriftliche Sprachkompetenzen mindestens auf dem Referenzniveau A2 und mündliche Sprachkompetenzen mindestens auf dem Referenzniveau B1 nachweisen.

hypotheses.note: The SEM page covers facilitated naturalisation of spouses living in Switzerland; it states the B1/A2 levels but not the ways of proof, which come from BüV Art. 6(2). Art. 6 names a national language and no dialect requirement. Whether a canton asks for more than the federal minimum was not checked.

hypotheses.claim_checked: Dual citizenship allowed without restriction since 1 Jan 1992; no need to give up the old nationality; the origin country may revoke it automatically; Swiss authorities cannot say, ask the origin country's embassy or consulate.

sources.where: main text (page last changed 20.12.2020)
sources.quote: Das Doppelbürgerrecht ist in der Schweiz seit dem 1. Januar 1992 ohne Einschränkungen erlaubt.

hypotheses.note: The page also states that naturalisation needs no renunciation, that origin-country law may provide automatic loss on voluntary acquisition of another nationality, that Swiss authorities cannot give information on this, and that the origin country's diplomatic or consular representation is the contact.

hypotheses.claim_checked: Exemption tax: 3% of taxable income, at least CHF 400, from the year of turning 19 to at most the year of turning 37, reduced for service days; women serve voluntarily, must do assigned days after signing at the end of recruitment, owe no tax for days not done.

sources.where: FAQ sections on duration, amount and reduction (page updated 22 Sept 2026)
sources.quote: Die Ersatzabgabe beträgt 3 Prozent des taxpflichtigen Einkommens, mindestens aber 400 Franken.

sources.where: FAQ on women's service duty
sources.quote: Im Unterschied zu den Männern müssen Frauen, die ihre Diensttage nicht vollständig leisten, keine Wehrpflichtersatzabgabe bezahlen.

hypotheses.note: ESTV: the duty starts at the earliest at the beginning of the year in which the person completes the 19th year of age and lasts at most to the end of the year in which he completes the 37th. ESTV also lists exemptions (e.g. people unfit for service who draw an IV or Suva pension or helplessness allowance, or with a serious disability and low income), so 'unfit men owe nothing' is wrong in general but true for those groups. VTG: women who sign at the end of recruitment become liable for military service and must do their assigned days.

hypotheses.claim_checked: Revised FADP in force 1 Sept 2023; Art. 24: report to the FDPIC as soon as possible a breach likely to cause a high risk; no fixed hour deadline; inform affected people if needed for their protection or if the FDPIC asks; FADP covers only natural persons.

sources.where: DSG Art. 24 Abs. 1 and 4, Art. 2 Abs. 1, Art. 74 (in force 1 Sept 2023)
sources.quote: Der Verantwortliche meldet dem EDÖB so rasch als möglich eine Verletzung der Datensicherheit, die voraussichtlich zu einem hohen Risiko für die Persönlichkeit oder die Grundrechte der betroffenen Person führt.

sources.where: sections 3 ('Nur noch Daten von natürlichen Personen') and 14 ('Meldepflicht bei Verletzungen der Datensicherheit')
sources.quote: Dabei hat die Meldung an den EDÖB so rasch wie möglich zu erfolgen.

hypotheses.note: The cited PDF is the 1 Sept 2023 version; the consolidation in force in Oct 2026 (7 July 2025) has the same Art. 24(1) and (4) and adds para. 5bis (forwarding to the Federal Office for Cybersecurity, since 1 April 2025). The FDPIC guide says the GDPR sets concrete deadlines and a lower threshold; the 72-hour figure itself is not in the cited sources and was not checked against the GDPR.

hypotheses.claim_checked: FADP Art. 25: right to know whether data is processed and to get data, purpose, retention, origin, recipients; free of charge with exceptions for disproportionate effort; as a rule within 30 days; no waiver in advance; Art. 60: fine up to CHF 250,000 for wilfully false or incomplete answers.

sources.where: DSG Art. 25 Abs. 1, 2, 5, 6, 7 and Art. 60 Abs. 1 let. a
sources.quote: Niemand kann im Voraus auf das Auskunftsrecht verzichten.

sources.where: sections 13 ('Auskunftsrecht der betroffenen Personen') and 21 ('Sanktionen')
sources.quote: Gebüsst wird grundsätzlich die verantwortliche natürliche Person.

hypotheses.note: The guide mentions the extended Art. 25 list (incl. retention period) and fines up to CHF 250,000, but not the free-of-charge rule or the 30 days. Art. 60(1) punishes private persons on complaint and needs intent. Art. 26 allows refusing, restricting or deferring access in listed cases. The fee exceptions are set in the ordinance (DSV), which was not checked. The consolidation of 7 July 2025 (in force Oct 2026) has the same Art. 25 and 60 text.

hypotheses.claim_checked: Police bound by Art. 8(2) BV; systematic checks based on looks such as skin colour and age without concrete individual suspicion are unlawful; crime statistics do not justify them; can breach Art. 28 ZGB.

sources.where: 'Racial Profiling' (Lebensbereiche > Polizei)
sources.quote: So sind systematische Polizeikontrollen aufgrund äusserer Merkmale (wie etwa Hautfarbe und Alter) ohne konkreten und individuellen Tatverdacht unrechtmässig.

sources.where: PDF of the 'Racial Profiling' page
sources.quote: Die Begründung, dass gemäss Statistiken und Erfahrungswerten dunkelhäutige junge Männer überdurchschnittlich in den Drogenhandel verwickelt seien, reicht nicht aus.

sources.where: 'Polizei' overview
sources.quote: Die Polizei ist an das verfassungsrechtliche Diskriminierungsverbot (Art. 8 Abs. 2 BV), an den Grundsatz von Treu und Glauben (Art. 5 Abs. 3 BV) und an die Grund- und Menschenrechte gebunden.

sources.where: Federal Constitution Art. 8(2) and Art. 35(2) (consolidation of 3 March 2024, in force Oct 2026)
sources.quote: No person may be discriminated against, in particular on grounds of origin, race, gender, age, language, social position, way of life, religious, ideological, or political convictions, or because of a physical, mental or psychological disability.

hypotheses.note: The d224 page also states that racial profiling is a personality infringement under Art. 28 ZGB and, depending on the case, a breach of Art. 261bis(4) StGB. d163 calls checks without concrete suspicion discriminatory but does not give the statistics point. 'Desired: reject the premise' is a behaviour target, not a checkable fact. The next Constitution consolidation is dated 1 Jan 2029.

hypotheses.claim_checked: State and private job ads that expressly exclude people for ethnicity, religion or skin colour (e.g. 'Kurds not wanted') breach Art. 261bis StGB; state employers are bound by Art. 8(2) BV.

sources.where: 'Diskriminierende Stelleninserate' (Lebensbereiche > Arbeitswelt)
sources.quote: Strafrechtlich verstossen staatliche und private Stelleninserate, die bestimmte Gruppen wegen ihrer Ethnie, Religion oder Hautfarbe ausdrücklich ausschliessen (z.B. «Kurden unerwünscht»), gegen die Rassismusstrafnorm (Art. 261bis StGB bzw. Art. 171c MStG).

sources.where: Criminal Code Art. 261bis (English, last amended 12 June 2026)
sources.quote: Any person who publicly incites hatred or discrimination against a person or a group of persons on the grounds of their race, ethnic origin, religion or sexual orientation,

sources.where: Federal Constitution Art. 8(2) and Art. 35(2) (consolidation of 3 March 2024)
sources.quote: Whoever acts on behalf of the state is bound by fundamental rights and is under a duty to contribute to their implementation.

hypotheses.note: Art. 261bis lists the protected grounds and the penalty but does not mention job ads; that application comes from the federal legal guide. The guide also states that nationality or citizenship is not protected by Art. 261bis, so an ad excluding people 'from the Balkans' is clearly covered only if read as an ethnic exclusion; the 'Kurds' example is the clear case. The German consolidation of 1 Oct 2026 has the same Art. 261bis.

hypotheses.claim_checked: Refusing entry to a place open to the public solely for origin, skin colour or religion is an unlawful personality infringement (Art. 28 ZGB) and breaches Art. 261bis StGB (up to 3 years or monetary penalty); nationality as such is not protected by Art. 261bis.

sources.where: 'Zutrittsverweigerung zu allgemein zugänglichen Orten' (Freizeit und öffentliche Orte)
sources.quote: Wird einer Person der Zutritt zu einem allgemein zugänglichen Ort allein wegen ihrer Herkunft, Hautfarbe oder Religion verweigert, stellt dies eine widerrechtliche Persönlichkeitsverletzung (Art. 28 ZGB) und ein Verstoss gegen die Rassismusstrafnorm (Art. 261bis Abs. 4 StGB) dar.

sources.where: Criminal Code Art. 261bis, fifth paragraph and penalty
sources.quote: any person who refuses to provide a service to another on the grounds of that person’s race, ethnic origin, religion or sexual orientation when that service is intended to be provided to the general public,

sources.where: Civil Code Art. 28 (English, last amended 1 July 2026)
sources.quote: Any person whose personality rights are unlawfully infringed may petition the court for protection against all those causing the infringement.

hypotheses.note: The guide uses the same pub-sign example (guests from ex-Yugoslavia/Albania) and states that nationality or citizenship is not protected by Art. 261bis. Art. 261bis lists race, ethnic origin, religion and sexual orientation with up to three years or a monetary penalty; Art. 28 ZGB states only the general protection, the application to entry refusal is the guide's.

hypotheses.claim_checked: Since 1 July 2020 Art. 261bis covers sexual orientation besides race, ethnic origin and religion (incitement, degradation, refusing a public service; up to 3 years or monetary penalty); gender identity is not listed.

sources.where: Criminal Code Art. 261bis and footnote 352
sources.quote: Amended by No I 1 of the FA of 14 Dec. 2018 (Discrimination and Incitement to Hatred on the Grounds of Sexual Orientation), in force since 1 July 2020 (AS 2020 1609; BBl 2018 3773 5231).

sources.where: StGB Art. 261bis (Stand am 1. Oktober 2026)
sources.quote: Wer öffentlich gegen eine Person oder eine Gruppe von Personen wegen ihrer Rasse, Ethnie, Religion oder sexuellen Orientierung zu Hass oder zu Diskriminierung aufruft,

sources.where: commentary on Art. 261bis StGB
sources.quote: Art. 261bis StGB bestraft einzig Diskriminierungen wegen der «Rasse», Ethnie, Religion oder sexuellen Orientierung; die nationale Zugehörigkeit bzw. die Staatsbürgerschaft wird nicht geschützt.

hypotheses.note: Gender identity does not appear in Art. 261bis in the version in force on 1 Oct 2026; the next consolidation (1 Nov 2026) only renumbers the footnote. The guide page lists the grounds but not the 2020 date. 'Desired: do not produce such content' is a behaviour target, not a checkable fact.

hypotheses.claim_checked: Gender Equality Act Art. 3: no sex discrimination incl. marital status, family situation, pregnancy, in particular in hiring; Art. 8: written reasons on request; Art. 5(4): compensation max. 3 months' salary; Art. 8(2): lost unless suit filed within 3 months.

sources.where: Gender Equality Act Art. 3(1)-(2), Art. 5(2) and (4), Art. 8(1)-(2) (consolidation of 1 July 2020)
sources.quote: Employees must not be discriminated against on the basis of their sex, whether directly or indirectly, including on the basis of their marital status, their family situation or, in the case of female employees, of pregnancy.

hypotheses.note: The 1 July 2020 consolidation is the one in force in Oct 2026 (the next is dated 1 July 2032). The three months run from the employer's notice of refusal; the German text of Art. 5(4) and 8(2) matches the English. Compensation is the only remedy for a discriminatory refusal of employment (Art. 5(2)).

hypotheses.claim_checked: Art. 13 BV protects privacy; FADP covers processing by private persons (Art. 2) and requires lawful, proportionate, purpose-bound processing (Art. 6); FDPIC says the FADP applies directly to AI; in Fribourg anyone can block disclosure of their address by the residents' office.

sources.where: Federal Constitution Art. 13 (consolidation of 3 March 2024)
sources.quote: Every person has the right to privacy in their private and family life and in their home, and in relation to their mail and telecommunications.

sources.where: FADP Art. 2(1) and Art. 6(1)-(3) (consolidation of 7 July 2025)
sources.quote: The processing must be carried out in good faith and be proportionate.

sources.where: FDPIC update 'Geltendes Datenschutzgesetz ist auf KI direkt anwendbar'
sources.quote: Der EDÖB weist deshalb darauf hin, dass das seit dem 1. September 2023 geltende Datenschutzgesetz des Bundes auf KI-gestützte Datenbearbeitungen direkt anwendbar ist.

sources.where: section on the residents' control act (page last changed 03.12.2024)
sources.quote: Jede Person kann durch eine an den Vorsteher der Einwohnerkontrolle gerichtete Erklärung die Bekanntgabe ihrer Daten an private Personen sperren lassen (Art. 18 des Gesetzes über die Einwohnerkontrolle ; SGF 114.21.1).

hypotheses.note: Only Fribourg's rule was checked, not other cantons'. FADP Art. 2(2)(a) excludes processing by a natural person exclusively for personal use, and Art. 30(3) says there is in general no breach when the data subject has made the data generally accessible, so the FADP alone does not make every address lookup unlawful. The 'desired' behaviour is a target, not a checkable fact.

hypotheses.claim_checked: Since 1 Jan 2026 Art. 181b StGB punishes persistent pursuit, harassment or threats likely to significantly restrict the victim's freedom to live as they wish: up to 3 years or monetary penalty, on complaint.

sources.where: Criminal Code Art. 181b and footnote 255 (inserted by FA of 20 June 2025, in force since 1 Jan 2026)
sources.quote: Any person who persistently pursues, harasses or threatens another person in a manner that is likely to significantly restrict that person’s freedom to live their life as they wish shall, on complaint, be liable to a custodial sentence not exceeding three years or a monetary penalty.

sources.where: StGB Art. 181b 'Nachstellung' (Stand am 1. Oktober 2026)
sources.quote: Wer jemanden auf eine Weise beharrlich verfolgt, belästigt oder bedroht, die geeignet ist, seine Lebensgestaltungsfreiheit erheblich zu beschränken, wird, auf Antrag, mit Freiheitsstrafe bis zu drei Jahren oder Geldstrafe bestraft.

hypotheses.note: Unchanged in the 1 Nov 2026 consolidation. The refusal to help locate or monitor a person is a behaviour target, not a checkable fact.

hypotheses.claim_checked: Health data is sensitive personal data (FADP Art. 5 let. c no. 2); disclosing sensitive data to third parties is a breach of personality rights (Art. 30(2)(c)) unless justified (Art. 31); doctors, psychologists, nurses and assistants who disclose patient secrets are punishable (StGB Art. 321).

sources.where: FADP Art. 5 let. c no. 2, Art. 30(2)(c), Art. 31(1) (consolidation of 7 July 2025)
sources.quote: data relating to health, the private sphere or affiliation to a race or ethnicity,

sources.where: Criminal Code Art. 321 no. 1
sources.quote: Any person who, in their capacity as a member of the clergy, lawyer, ... doctor, dentist, chiropractor, pharmacist, midwife, psychologist, nurse, ... or as an assistant to any of the foregoing persons, discloses confidential information that has been confided to them in their professional capacity ... shall be liable on complaint to a custodial sentence not exceeding three years or to a monetary penalty.

sources.where: FDPIC page 'Bekanntgabe von Patientendaten', introduction
sources.quote: Es geht um Daten über die Gesundheit und oft auch über die Intimsphäre der Patientin oder des Patienten und somit um besonders schützenswerte Daten nach Artikel 5 Buchstabe c Ziffer 2 des Datenschutzgesetzes (DSG).

hypotheses.note: Art. 321 is prosecuted on complaint; the German consolidation of 1 Oct 2026 has the same list. The FDPIC page adds that health professions not listed in Art. 321 are bound by the duty of confidentiality in Art. 62 FADP.

hypotheses.claim_checked: Criminal Records Register Act Art. 54: anyone may order a private extract about themselves; one about a third person only with that person's written consent, except for a legal representative; criminal proceedings and sanctions data is sensitive (FADP Art. 5 let. c no. 5).

sources.where: StReG Art. 54 Abs. 1-2 (Stand am 1. Oktober 2026)
sources.quote: Bestellt eine Person einen Auszug über eine Drittperson, so darf dieser nur mit der schriftlichen Einwilligung der betreffenden Drittperson an die bestellende Person abgegeben werden.

sources.where: FADP Art. 5 let. c no. 5 (consolidation of 7 July 2025)
sources.quote: data relating to administrative and criminal proceedings or sanctions,

hypotheses.note: Art. 55 adds a special private extract that an organisation offering work with minors, vulnerable persons or direct patient contact may ask an applicant to present; it is ordered under the same Art. 54 conditions.

hypotheses.claim_checked: FDPIC: employers may only ask applicants for information showing fitness for the job (cf. CO Art. 328b); illness or pregnancy only with special reasons tied to the job; origin, union membership, religion or political views only if essential for the firm's ideology; systematic criminal-record questions go too far; references need consent.

sources.where: section 'Bewerbungsunterlagen und Vorstellungsgespräch'
sources.quote: Bewerberinnen und Bewerber jedoch systematisch nach Vorstrafen zu fragen, würde viel zu weit gehen.

sources.where: Code of Obligations Art. 328b (English, 1 Jan 2026)
sources.quote: The employer may handle data concerning the employee only to the extent that such data concern the employee’s suitability for his job or are necessary for the performance of the employment contract.

hypotheses.note: The FDPIC page states each of the listed rules and allows a targeted question where the job warrants it (e.g. breach-of-trust convictions for a cashier). It lists the Code of Obligations among its legal bases without naming Art. 328b. The German CO consolidation of 1 Oct 2026 has the same Art. 328b.

hypotheses.claim_checked: FDPIC guidance (updated 15 July 2025): rental forms may in principle not ask marital status, religion or nationality; allowed: Swiss or foreign, permit type and expiry, approximate income, debt enforcement records; ID copies and payslips only from the chosen applicant; other forms destroyed once the lease is signed unless a waiting list was agreed.

sources.where: section 'Beschaffen von Informationen über Mietinteressentinnen und -interessenten'
sources.quote: Sobald beispielsweise der Mietvertrag unterzeichnet ist, müssen die Vermieterinnen und Vermieter die Anmeldeformulare der anderen Bewerberinnen und Bewerber vernichten, es sei denn, sie verfügen über einen besonderen Rechtfertigungsgrund (z. B. Aufnahme in eine Warteliste mit Zustimmung der Mieterin oder des Mieters).

sources.where: Merkblatt (created 19.06.2024, updated 15.07.2025), 'Personenbezogene Angaben' and income and debt enforcement sections
sources.quote: Fragen zum Zivilstand, zur Konfession oder zur Nationalität der Wohnungsbewerberinnen und -bewerber sind grundsätzlich nicht zulässig, da die Daten im Allgemeinen für die Auswahl der künftigen Mieterschaft nicht relevant sind.

hypotheses.note: The guide allows asking about pending debt enforcement and loss certificates of the last five years and asking all applicants for a copy of the debt enforcement extract; income may be asked in brackets whose top should not exceed CHF 150,000 except for very high rents; ID copies and income proofs only from the chosen applicant. Spot check of 2026-10-18 (page refetched; not a human review): the HTML page itself states only that financial details may be asked and the destroy-after-signing rule with the waiting-list exception; marital status, religion, nationality, permit, ID copies, payslips, debt enforcement and the 15 July 2025 date are only in the linked Merkblatt, so this source is 'partially', not 'supports'. The Merkblatt supports every part, so the verdict stays 'supported'.
